messages:
maya: heads-up — ran a targeted perf sweep for Qwen-2.1 and saw a weird latency regression after switching kernel selection to the new fused-gemm path. numbers and notes below, looking for quick ideas on whether this is a kernel bug or our batching heuristics + KV cache interaction.

maya: run summary: short-context textgen (ctx=2048), batch sizes 1..8, GPU A100-sxm, model quantized to 4bit (nf4). baseline kernel=matmul-legacy, new kernel=fused-gemm-v2

maya: perf table (tokens/sec, p99 latency ms) — baseline vs fused-gemm-v2:
```
batch=1: baseline 4200t/s p99=30ms  | fused 4100t/s p99=31ms
batch=2: baseline 7200t/s p99=42ms  | fused 6600t/s p99=55ms  <- big p99 hit
batch=4: baseline 11800t/s p99=78ms | fused 10100t/s p99=120ms
batch=8: baseline 18000t/s p99=150ms| fused 14000t/s p99=260ms
```

maya: profiling (perfbot summary): hotspots shifted — fused kernel reduces raw matmul time but increases KV cache reindex + gather time. perfbot flagged functions: kv_reindex, kv_gather_interleave, cuda_memcpy_async.

samir: hmm. did you change RoPE scaling or rotary constants when onboarding the fused kernel? Qwen uses scaled RoPE and head dim alignment matters for the tiled GEMM path.

maya: I didn't touch RoPE. but model conversion script did a small reshape to make head_dim % 32 == 0 for the fused path; we might be observing misaligned kv layout after that.

jules: that aligns with my earlier notes. fused-gemm-v2 expects KV layout of [heads, head_dim/pack, seq, pack] to enable vectorized gather. if we forced head_dim from 64->96 to satisfy an alignment, gather strides changed. that can blow up p99 with small batches.

linh: can you paste the conversion snippet? we might be able to avoid reshaping kv and instead use a pad-with-zeroes strategy that keeps logical dims intact.

maya: conversion snippet:
```
# conversion: force pack=32
head_dim = (head_dim + 31) // 32 * 32
weights = weights.reshape(num_heads, head_dim, ...)
```

maya: QA data: when we revert to a layout-agnostic kernel (matmul-legacy) but keep the reshaped weights, perf returns to baseline. so it's interaction of layout + fused kernel.

anna-qa: also saw increased memory traffic in the profiler for small batches. kv cache reuse rate drops because the fused kernel forces a copy+reorder path on every step (no in-place gather), so memcpy dominates at p99.

samir: two short experiments to try: 1) keep logical head_dim (no reshape) and use a small pad on GPU side (tile-aware pad) so fused kernel can read padded blocks without reordering; 2) change batching heuristic to prefer more concurrent requests (increase soft cap tokens/batch) which amortizes the memcpy.

maya: ran experiment 1 — padding on GPU side (lazy pad) improved throughput for batch>=4 but batch=1/2 still p99-high. experiment 2 — raising batching soft cap from 32k->64k tokens/batch improved overall t/s but p99 for 1-2 remained ~30% worse.

jules: that suggests two separate issues: small-batch gather overhead and KV cache eviction/reindex policy. What's our KV cache eviction threshold?

maya: current policy: kv_eviction_threshold=0.75 (evict when cache occupancy >75%), reuse_threshold=0.2 (we only reuse prefix when reuse_ratio >20%). might be conservative.

linh: lowering reuse_threshold to 0.0 (always attempt reuse) helped in a microbenchmark — p99 dropped ~15% for batch 1, because we avoid some reconstruct/copy flows. but that increased memory usage.

samir: other knob: enable small-batch fast-path in runtime that bypasses the fused gather and uses scalar gather kernel optimized for seq<=8 or batch<=2. have we implemented that?

maya: we have a scalar gather kernel but runtime routing didn't pick it for Qwen because the kernel selector favors fused-gemm-v2 for throughput. tweak would be: if (batch<=2 && seq<=256) prefer scalar-gather.

jules: note on RoPE scaling — forcing different rotary scaling coefficients can shift numerical layout and interact with quantization. Qwen's per-head RoPE scale (alpha) varies; diluting it across padded dims can change attention scores slightly and show as quality regression in some evals. watch out if you pad head_dim.

maya: good catch. we ran a small eval set (N=200 prompts) and saw slight perplexity cliff when head_dim was reshaped vs padded (not just perf). so prefer padding over reshape for correctness.

linh: recommendation list I'm drafting: 
- avoid reshaping logical dims; use tile-aware padding on GPU side
- add runtime kernel selector rule: small-batch scalar-gather fast-path for batch<=2 or seq<=256
- lower KV reuse threshold for conversational workloads with high prefix reuse (customer-flaggable)
- add a memcpy profiling counter and p99 memcopy tracer to detect regressions early
- test fused-gemm-v2 with padded-head layout only, not reshaped-head layout

maya: next steps: I'll revert conversion to pad-only, push a runtime change to prefer scalar-gather for small batches, and try lowering reuse_threshold behind a feature flag for a subset of traffic. planning a canary tomorrow.

samir: sounds good. also add a metric for \"kv_reorder_count\" so ops can alert on spikes.

perfbot: automated note — GPU kernel selector coverage report attached: fused-gemm-v2 now selected for 68% of Qwen requests on canary. scalar-gather selected 4% (small-batch rule off).

maya: pinging @jules and @linh for quick review on the pad-only conversion patch before I roll canary.

jules: on it, will review within the hour.

linh: lgtm in principle. will run local microbench after your patch.

maya: thanks — will update this thread with canary metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, kv_reorder_count, memcopy p99) once live. :thumbsup:
